<reason>PRO clarified opt-in as one separable, scoped upfront yes covering all languages, defeating CON's forty-negotiations paralysis claim while preserving human dubbing and access. PRO's dilemma was decisive: if a performer cannot refuse the AI rider and still work it is not consent, and if they can, that is opt-in. CON repeatedly claimed existing boilerplate already requires specific consent, conceding the substance, and never squarely answered the reputational injury of fabricated performances.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>Side A's response to the pressure questions and Rebuttal 1: distinguishing creating new utterances from colorization/upscaling, and showing refusal blocks only reuse of the biometric model, not distribution, sequels, or translation.</best_rebuttal>
